To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the variant frequency in untreated C57Bl mice is about 2.8 x 10(-6), while it is 3.0 x 10(-4) in untreated NMRI and about 6 x 10(-3) in untreated DBA/2J animals.

the frequencies of 6-thio-guanine-resistant cells are higher in the mouse strain DBA than in C57Bl or NMRI, that ethylnitroso urea induces a dose-related increase of variant frequencies, while cyclophosphamid does not, and that the variant frequencies in the mouse strain C57Bl are lower than in the other strains.

the variant frequencies for 8-azaguanine- and 6-thiouguanine-resistant cells in spleen cells of mice without treatment and after treatment with ethylnituosourea and cyclosphosphamide are strain dependent and that cyclosphosphmide treatment of mice does not result in a dose-response relationship for the frequency of 6-thioquanine resistant spleen cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sensitive and specific in vivo assay for the detection of mutagenic effects on the hematopoietic system.
the development of a method for the detection of in vivo-induced mutations in mice by the use of the 6-thiopurine system.
the estimation of the spontaneous mutation rate of the HGPRT locus in mouse strains and the influence of chemical mutagens on the frequency of mutant cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the variant frequencies for 7-thioguanin-resistant cells in different mouse strain can be estimated by the method of autoradiography, but that the results obtained with cyclophosphamid are difficult to interpret.
no clear-cut dose-response relationship can be established for cyclophosphamidetreated mice.
the variant frequency of 6-thioG-resistant spleen cells can be increased in mice by in vivo exposure to ethylnitrousourea and cyclopohosphamide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
6-thiobutanol, which has been shown to inhibit the metabolism of 6-thio-guanine, is an effective tool for the selective enrichment of thioguanine-resistant lymphocytes in mouse spleen cells.
the frequencies of 6-thioG resistant spleen cells in mice are not increased after exposure to cyclophos-phamide but are increased after exposure to ethylnitrourea.
6-thiopurines are suitable for the detection of induced mutation frequencies in mouse strains with different genetic backgrounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to detect a small but measurable effect of cyclophosphamidine on the mutation rate.
we need to be careful when interpreting data from animal models of cancer.
